Babies born to mothers with anaemia have smaller brains, particularly in key regions linked to movement, learning and the regulation of emotion, according to a study.

Researchers said the differences, first detected at the age of one, could lead to cognitive problems when children started school.

The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.

The petition will be lodged with Charles, Jamaica’s head of state, on Monday.

The pay increases add more than 60% to what are already the world’s highest ministerial salaries.

rfi.description: Twelve countries, including Britain, Canada and France, said on Tuesday that they would impose sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, following an increase in attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the occupied territory.

rfi.title: French pupils fall to record low in global education survey
rfi.description: French students' results in the 2025 international Pisa survey are the lowest ever recorded, yet remain in line with the OECD average, according to results published on Tuesday. French Education Minister Édouard Geffray criticised social media as one of the causes, and pledged to focus on raising standards in middle schools over the next five-year term in order to close the gap.

rfi.title: Internal inquiry opened after Eiffel Tower 'sexist' closure prompts strike
rfi.description: The Eiffel Tower reopened on Tuesday after staff walked out over the removal of women colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group which later apologised. The operating company has acknowledged it was wrong to accept the conditions and has opened an internal investigation.

rfi.title: Hunt on for thieves after Renoir museum raid in southern France
rfi.description: A search is under way for the thieves who stole several paintings from a museum dedicated to the French Impressionist painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir in the south of France in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

rfi.title: French firefighters begin six-week strike over funding after record summer fires
rfi.description: French professional firefighters launch a six-week nationwide campaign on Tuesday, demanding more funding, staff and better protection for their health after a summer of unprecedented wildfires.

rfi.title: France tries 14 over deadliest Channel migrant crossing disaster
rfi.description: Fourteen people are to go on trial in France on Tuesday over the loss of 31 people including a seven-year-old child in 2021, in the deadliest small-boat crossing accident recorded in the Channel.

rfi.description: The fallout from the AfD’s landslide in Saxony-Anhalt is testing Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s reform agenda, Germany’s support for Ukraine and the political firewall designed to keep the far-right out of power.

rfi.title: EU chief unveils €200m Greenland package amid tensions over Trump claims
rfi.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen unveiled a 200-million-euro investment package for Greenland during the second of a two-day visit. The European Union has increased its focus on the vast, strategic island since President Donald Trump began insisting that the United States should take control of it for security reasons.

rfi.title: Sons of Yemen ex-president on trial in France over alleged stolen assets
rfi.description: Two sons of former Yemeni president Ali Abdullah Saleh are on trial in Paris on Monday, accused of embezzling public funds that were used to buy luxury property worth €16 million in Paris.

rfi.title: Jamaica steps up slavery reparations campaign with petition to King Charles III
rfi.description: Jamaica is testing a new legal route in its long-running campaign for slavery reparations, asking Britain’s monarch to put key questions before the Privy Council.

rfi.description: France and South Korea will invest one billion euros to support the audiovisual and entertainment sector, President Emmanuel Macron said as he brought together some of the world's top entertainment bosses for a summit on the future of cinema.

rfi.title: Far-right activists stand trial in Paris over killing of rugby star Aramburu
rfi.description: Two far-right activists go on trial in Paris on Monday over the 2022 killing of former Argentina rugby international Federico Martin Aramburu, who was shot dead following a late-night altercation in the French capital.

rfi.title: Global film industry gathers in France to tackle 'unprecedented challenges'
rfi.description: Some 200 cinema and entertainment professionals from around the world are gathering in the south of France on Monday to discuss the future of creative sectors threatened by artificial intelligence, streaming and competition from online platforms.

rfi.title: Visa Pour l'Image: Tato wins top prize for Madagascar protest coverage
rfi.description: AFP photographer Luis Tato on Saturday won the top award at the prestigious Visa Pour l'Image photojournalism festival in Perpignan, southern France.

rfi.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday for talks with the Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky a day after meeting the Russian president Vladimir Putin to discuss proposals over how to end the four-year war between Russia and Ukraine.

euronews.title: Europe Today: Ceuta cries out for EU help, Hungary expels 10 Russian diplomats
euronews.description: Ceuta's mayor Juan Jesús Vivas has requested greater European support for the continuing crisis in the Spanish enclave after 80.000 crossed the border illegally last month. Meanwhile, the Hungarian government has decided to expel 10 Russian diplomats over "unacceptable" activities.

euronews.title: Norway bids farewell to King Harald V, 'grandfather' of the nation
euronews.description: Embodying an open and tolerant Norway, the king made a deep impression by celebrating diversity in a 2016 speech marking the 25th anniversary of his reign.

euronews.title: The Russian exception: Why Moscow still has a role in Europe’s ITER fusion project despite EU sanctions
euronews.description: EU-Russia tensions collide with decades of scientific cooperation at ITER, the world’s largest nuclear fusion experiment. As fusion becomes a strategic EU priority, Brussels faces a dilemma over its continued reliance on Russian expertise and technology.

euronews.title: At least five killed in large-scale overnight Russian aerial attack on Ukraine's capital
euronews.description: Elsewhere in Ukraine, a Russian drone strike killed civilians at a checkpoint on the border with Moldova, the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine said on Wednesday.

euronews.title: Possible massacre and cannibalism 7,000 years ago uncovered in Granada
euronews.description: Analysis of nearly 1,000 bones found in three caves in Granada shows that cannibalism was a recurring Neolithic practice, with signs of collective violence, possible rituals and skulls turned into containers.

euronews.title: Delay tactic or genuine solution? Carbon capture under fire again as EU invests in ‘unproven’ technology
euronews.description: Carbon capture and storage has been found to be “technically uncertain and very high cost”.

euronews.title: Getting those steps in does reduce the risk of early death. But it is also the pace that matters
euronews.description: It is not only the number of steps per day but also the walking pace that matters for lowering the risk of early death, according to new research.

euronews.title: Why a 50% harvest collapse won't leave shelves short of Champagne
euronews.description: France’s Champagne region is facing an extraordinary harvest collapse. Yet consumers should not expect the number of bottles reaching shops to halve — at least not yet.

euronews.description: Premium economy is getting an upgrade as airlines make flying more private, comfortable and luxurious – just without the hefty business class price tag.

euronews.description: The National Air Traffic Services (NATS) said late on Tuesday it was still working to resolve disruption following a "system issue."

euronews.title: Croatia on wheels: The great Adriatic motorhome route
euronews.description: On a 25-day road trip we travel along a coastline of striking contrasts, from Roman cities and Venetian towns to pebble beaches, islands and roads overlooking some of Europe's most spectacular scenery.

euronews.title: A European Central Bank rate hike is all but certain, the reasoning less so
euronews.description: The European Central Bank is all but certain to raise interest rates on Thursday, with investors pricing the move at near-total probability, but the decision is more awkward than the numbers suggest as inflation is being driven almost entirely by energy with underlying pressures actually easing.

euronews.title: US destroys five Iranian tankers as Tehran launches retaliatory strikes on Jordan
euronews.description: US military says it destroyed five more Iranian oil tankers after missile attacks on a Navy warship. Iran struck a US military base in Jordan with missiles in retaliation, the Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday. Jordan's army said it shot down 18 missiles from Iran targeting the kingdom.

euronews.description: Lior Raz, one of the show's creators, told Netflix's Tudum site that he hoped viewers would understand "how peace is important, and how we need to think differently and how war is ruining the universe."

euronews.title: 'Turning blind eye' to AfD win further angers voters, political scientist warns
euronews.description: Chancellor Merz's government must recognise the far-right AfD's victory in Saxony-Anhalt and voter discontent that led to the win, or further cement its downfall, an expert on East German politics warned.

euronews.title: Ceuta President urges the EU to take firm action against Morocco, as the city is 'on the brink of collapse'
euronews.description: Juan Jesús Vivas accused Rabat of pursuing a “harassment policy” aimed at suffocating the exclave, while the Spanish government and the EU continue to regard Morocco as a trusted partner in addressing irregular migration.

euronews.title: UAE warned Netanyahu of 7 October attack, Israeli newspaper reports
euronews.description: Israeli Premier Benjamin Netanyahu is facing a political storm and accusations in the middle of Israel’s election campaign that he ignored a direct warning from the UAE about the imminence of Hamas’ 7 October attack in 2023.

lemonde.title: Aux Etats-Unis, Donald Trump se place au cœur de la campagne républicaine avant les midterms
lemonde.description: Le président américain interviendra mercredi au premier jour de la convention républicaine, qui se tiendra à Dallas, au Texas, les 9 et 10 septembre, avant des élections de mi-mandat qui s’annoncent indécises.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Edouard Philippe prend l’initiative du rassemblement de la droite et du centre en proposant une rencontre début novembre
lemonde.description: Celui qui espère s’imposer comme le candidat unique a annoncé mardi qu’il allait envoyer un courrier à ses concurrents, et plusieurs figures allant de François Bayrou à David Lisnard, pour travailler à l’union. Bruno Retailleau a d’ores et déjà balayé la proposition.

lemonde.title: En Israël, les révélations sur l’alerte reçue par Benyamin Nétanyahou avant le 7-Octobre provoquent un séisme politique
lemonde.description: Un livre à paraître assure que le premier ministre israélien aurait été informé « que le chef du Hamas à Gaza, Yahya Sinouar, planifiait une opération majeure contre Israël » par le président des Emirats arabes unis dix jours avant l’attaque.

lemonde.title: Onze pays européens et le Canada imposent à Israël des sanctions contre les produits issus des colonies en Cisjordanie
lemonde.description: Dans le sillage du Royaume-Uni, la France, le Danemark, l’Espagne, la Finlande, l’Irlande, l’Islande, la Norvège, la Pologne, le Portugal et la Suède ainsi qu’Ottawa ont opté pour une logique de sanctions contre l’ensemble des colonies.

lemonde.title: Au procès de l’assassinat de Federico Martin Aramburu, les deux accusés confrontés à leur passé de violence
lemonde.description: Loïk Le Priol et Romain Bouvier comparaissent devant la cour d’assises de Paris depuis lundi 7 septembre pour avoir abattu l’ancien joueur de rugby, en mars 2022. Tous deux étaient membres du Groupe union défense, syndicat étudiant d’extrême droite, avant sa dissolution en 2024.

lemonde.title: OpenAI dit avoir résolu un problème de maths majeur mais crée des vagues
lemonde.description: Le créateur de ChatGPT a annoncé, mardi, qu’un de ses modèles d’intelligence artificielle avait résolu l’équation dite de Navier-Stokes, qui décrit l’écoulement des fluides.

lemonde.title: Olivier Bouygues et cinq de ses employés devant la justice pour avoir abattu des espèces protégées
lemonde.description: Le tribunal correctionnel d’Orléans jugeait lundi et mardi l’homme d’affaires ainsi que deux régisseurs et trois gardes-chasse pour des faits ayant eu lieu dans sa propriété de Sologne, à La Ferté-Saint-Aubin. Cinq ans de prison avec sursis et 750 000 euros d’amende ont été requis contre le milliardaire.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : deux morts dans une attaque de drones russes à la frontière entre l’Ukraine et la Moldavie
lemonde.description: Une attaque de drones russes sur le poste-frontière routier de Starokojache a tué deux personnes et en a blessé trois autres dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi, a fait savoir le gouverneur de la région d’Odessa, Oleh Kiper.

lemonde.title: Les déboires de Tudigo, la plateforme de financement participatif : plus de 26 000 investisseurs et près de 700 actionnaires piégés par une « guerre des chefs »
lemonde.description: La plateforme bordelaise s’est déclarée en cessation de paiements, fin juillet, et a été placée en redressement judiciaire, début août. Ses difficultés économiques ont été aggravées par un conflit entre ses deux dirigeants fondateurs, qui a pris en tenailles clients, actionnaires et salariés.

lemonde.title: L’Iran bombarde des bases en Jordanie et dans le Golfe, en riposte aux attaques des Etats-Unis contre des pétroliers iraniens
lemonde.description: Les gardiens de la révolution iraniens ont « pris pour cible deux navires américains et huit pétroliers présents dans la zone, leur infligeant des dégâts considérables », ont-ils affirmé dans un communiqué. Dix autres navires auraient été visés.

lemonde.title: Tensions commerciales : le Canada riposte aux surtaxes américaines, Washington surenchérit
lemonde.description: Le Canada affirme avoir calibré ses nouveaux droits de douane pour répondre, « au dollar près », à ceux imposés depuis le 22 août par son voisin du Sud. En réaction, la Maison Blanche a surenchéri, mardi soir, en annonçant de nouvelles surtaxes.

lemonde.title: PISA 2025 : le récit du « déclinisme français » de retour dans la présidentielle
lemonde.description: Les mauvais résultats de la France à l’enquête PISA – qui mesure le niveau scolaire des élèves de 15 ans – relancent les interrogations sur l’état du pays. Le thème du « déclin » de la France, bien qu’il ne soit pas nouveau, risque de s’installer au cœur de l’élection présidentielle de 2027.

lemonde.title: Au Royaume-Uni, une panne du contrôle aérien « très complexe » a provoqué des annulations de vols en cascade
lemonde.description: L’organisme britannique chargé du contrôle aérien a assuré avoir résolu le dysfonctionnement, mais au moins 177 vols ont encore été annulés mercredi, contre environ 1 300 la veille, selon le site de suivi du trafic aérien Flightradar24.

lemonde.title: Les sapeurs-pompiers de nouveau déçus après la présentation du projet de loi sur la modernisation de la sécurité civile
lemonde.description: Au sortir d’une réunion Place Beauvau, mardi, une intersyndicale a estimé que les mesures envisagées par le gouvernement ne répondaient à aucun des enjeux chers à la profession.

lemonde.title: « A cœur, l’amant », de LiIy King, est un faux « campus novel » et un vrai hommage au pouvoir de la fiction
lemonde.description: L’écrivaine américaine raconte la vie d’une étudiante en lettres, puis la revisite quelques décennies plus tard. Un roman empli d’espoir et de nostalgie.

lemonde.title: « South Park » rebaptisé « South America » : la série satirique raille les changements de noms voulus par Donald Trump
lemonde.description: Les créateurs de la série se moquent aussi des géants Apple et Google, qui ont adopté, sur leurs cartes américaines, les nouvelles appellations attribuées par le président à plusieurs lieux, comme le lac Ontario.

Wetter: Wann in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern Gewitter drohen
Leute: Chris Rock: Rückkehr zu den Oscars nur unter einer Bedingung
Handelsstreit: USA verhängen Einfuhrverbot für Milchprodukte und Alkohol aus Kanada
zeit.description: Nach dem Inkrafttreten kanadischer Gegenzölle untersagen die USA den Import bestimmter kanadischer Produkte. Auch US-Behörden sollen auf Waren aus Kanada verzichten.

zeit.title: Elbvertiefung: Der tägliche Newsletter aus Hamburg: Was an Hamburgs Schulen schief läuft
zeit.description: Die Elbvertiefung am Mittwoch – Mit einer Demo gegen Rechtsextremismus am Samstag, mehr Platz im Volksparkstadion und den Sorgen der Ehrbaren Kaufleute

zeit.title: Die Folgen von 9/11: Hat 9/11 Donald Trump erst ermöglicht?
zeit.description: Sind Donald Trump und diese USA Folgen der Anschläge des 11. September? In einem Spezial unseres US-Podcasts blicken wir auf den Tag, der die USA für immer veränderte.

zeit.title: Bundeszwang: Wann der Bund in Sachsen-Anhalt eingreifen könnte
zeit.description: Deutschland diskutiert über den Bundeszwang. Was kann der Bund tun, wenn eine Landesregierung gegen das Grundgesetz verstößt? Und: Wie ernst Putin die Verhandlungen meint

zeit.title: Staatliche Hilfen für Familien: Mit diesem Geld können Familien rechnen
zeit.description: Jedes Jahr lassen Eltern Millionen Euro an staatlichen und kommunalen Hilfen ungenutzt, weil sie nichts von deren Existenz wissen. Dabei gibt es weit mehr als Kindergeld.

zeit.title: 9/11-Attentäter: Die Täter und der Hass
zeit.description: Nach 9/11 hat Amerika nur einen Feind vor Augen. Die Jagd auf die Attentäter führt nach Afghanistan und Hamburg. Zu Osama bin Laden und Mohammed Atta. Wer waren sie?

france24fr.title: Massacres du 7-Octobre: "Nétanyahou savait"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mercredi 9 septembre, les réactions à la décision de douze pays, dont la France et le Royaume-Uni, de sanctionner les colonies israéliennes. Israël, où Haaretz maintient que Nétanyahou avait été informé de l’attaque du Hamas avant le 7 octobre 2023. Les réactions, en France, à la publication du nouveau classement Pisa. Les élèves français dégringolent – mais ils ne sont pas les seuls. La mort du papa de Casimir. Et une facétie des créateurs de «South Park».

france24fr.title: Ligue des champions : Kylian Mbappé et le Real Madrid résistent à l'Inter
france24fr.description: Le Real Madrid a remporté le choc de cette première soirée de Ligue des champions face à l’Inter (2-1). Auteur de l'ouverture du score, Kylian Mbappé est désormais le 5e meilleur buteur de l'histoire de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Premier sommet spatial international à Paris, l'Europe cherche à trouver sa place
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron réunit mercredi et jeudi à Paris le premier sommet spatial international, un rendez-vous boudé par SpaceX et Blue Origin. La question du multilatéralisme sera au cœur des discussions, alors que l'Europe de l'espace doit trouver sa place entre les géants américains et chinois.

france24fr.title: Le conflit entre les États-Unis et le Canada s'envenime : Trump interdit des produits canadiens
france24fr.description: Au travers de décrets présidentiels, la Maison Blanche a interdit, mardi, l'importation de certains produits canadiens, notamment des alcools, et relevé les droits de douane sur d'autres marchandises – avec une surtaxe de 50 % à compter du 15 septembre.

france24fr.title: Départ de Lonnie Bunch, le chef de la Smithsonian Institution dans le viseur de Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Premier Afro-Américain à diriger la Smithsonian Institution, Lonnie Bunch, a annoncé mardi son départ à la retraite. Il survient alors que l'administration Trump a multiplié les attaques à l'encontre du vaste complexe muséal.

france24fr.title: En direct : les États-Unis frappent des pétroliers iraniens, l'Iran cible une base américaine en Jordanie
france24fr.description: Les Gardiens de la révolution ont dit mercredi avoir attaqué une base militaire des États-Unis en Jordanie, ainsi qu'une vingtaine de bateaux dans le Golfe, en représailles à des frappes américaines qui ont détruit cinq navires pétroliers dans la région du Golfe. Au Yémen, les rebelles houthis soutenus par l'Iran font état, quant à eux, de plus de 30 frappes saoudiennes dans plusieurs régions. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Affaire des assistants du MoDem : Bayrou de retour devant la justice
france24fr.description: Tout part de soupçons sur l'utilisation d'assistants parlementaires européens au profit du MoDem, révélés par Corinne Lepage. En 2024, le procès en première instance aboutit à plusieurs condamnations mais François Bayrou est relaxé. Deux ans plus tard, l'affaire revient devant la justice en appel.

france24fr.title: Ligue des champions : Lille s'incline face au Betis Séville
france24fr.description: Lille a raté ses retrouvailles avec la Ligue des champions, menant deux fois avant de s'incliner et de finir à dix face au Betis Séville (3-2), mardi. En mal de points, les joueurs de Davide Ancelotti auront fort à faire face au géant Arsenal, le 13 octobre à Londres.

france24fr.title: Devant l'Assemblée, le Premier ministre sénégalais présente son plan pour redresser l'économie
france24fr.description: C'était ce mardi le grand oral du Premier ministre sénégalais Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo, qui a fait sa déclaration de politiques générales devant l'Assemblée nationale, acquise en majorité au Pastef d'Ousmane Sonko. Al Aminou Lo  a évoqué l'accord avec le FMI et promet de redresser l'économie du Sénégal, mais parle aussi de sacrifices. La correspondance à Dakar d'Elimane Ndao.

france24fr.title: Jean-Michel Blanquer : "Il ne faut pas être fataliste" face au classement Pisa de la France
france24fr.description: Menée dans 91 pays dont 38 de l’OCDE, la dernière enquête Pisa montre un abaissement général du niveau des élèves, notamment en France. Pour l'ancien ministre de l’Éducation nationale Jean-Michel Blanquer, les écrans et les réseaux sociaux ont une responsabilité dans ces résultats. Mais – pointe celui qui est aussi président du Laboratoire de la République – "tout en étant conscients du problème, il ne faut pas être fataliste".

france24fr.title: Droits de douane américains : la riposte du Canada entre en vigueur
france24fr.description: Les nouveaux droits de douane canadiens sont entrés en vigueur : environ 20 milliards de dollars d'importations en provenance des États-Unis sont désormais surtaxés. Il s'agit d'une riposte aux mesures décidées fin août par les États-Unis.

france24fr.title: Du Groënland aux Antilles : la carte des Etats-Unis selon Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Sur son réseau social, Donald Trump a publié une fausse carte des Etats-Unis sur laquelle le drapeau américain recouvre d'autres pays comme le Canada, le Groënland, le Mexique et incluant même les Antilles françaises. De quoi susciter la colère de certains états concernés et relancer le débat sur la santé mentale du président, face à la frénésie avec laquelle il publie des visuels mensongers.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie : trois questions autour des sanctions occidentales contre les colonies israéliennes
france24fr.description: Douze pays, dont la France, le Royaume-Uni et le Canada, ont indiqué mardi vouloir imposer des restrictions de commerce sur les biens issus des colonies israéliennes implantées en Cisjordanie occupée. France 24 fait le point sur les questions qui se posent après cette annonce.

france24fr.title: Le Canada peut-il résister à Trump ?
france24fr.description: La guerre commerciale s’intensifie entre le Canada et les États-Unis. Ottawa riposte aux nouveaux droits de douane américains imposés en août par Washington avec des surtaxes sur plusieurs produits importés des États-Unis. Le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney a averti que cette stratégie, visant à réduire la dépendance de son pays à l’égard des États-Unis, aurait néanmoins un "coût" économique à court terme.

france24fr.title: Kenya : les petits commerçants étrangers menacés d'expulsion
france24fr.description: 🇰🇪 Des milliers de Burundais cherchent à quitter le Kenya après l’annonce du président William Ruto de fermer les petits commerces tenus par des étrangers. Se sentant visés, ils affluent depuis lundi à leur ambassade à Nairobi.

france24fr.title: 11-Septembre : des milliers de documents sur la toxicité de l'air à New York rendus publics
france24fr.description: Le maire de New York Zohran Mamdani a annoncé mardi la publication en ligne de dizaines de milliers de documents montrant "ce que la ville savait de la présence d'air toxique" après le 11-Septembre. Ces documents pourraient mettre en cause deux de ses prédécesseurs : Rudy Giuliani, en poste au moment des attaques, puis Michael Bloomberg.

france24fr.title: Douze pays veulent sanctionner les colonies israéliennes en Cisjordanie occupée
france24fr.description: Le chef de la diplomatie israélienne a annoncé mardi la fermeture du consulat britannique à Jérusalem. Douze pays dont le Royaume-Uni avaient annoncé des sanctions contre les colonies israéliennes en Cisjordanie. Le secrétaire d'État américain Marco Rubio a déploré les "tensions en Cisjordanie" occupée mais a exclu que les États-Unis prennent des sanctions comparables.

france24fr.title: Ballon d'or : Mbappé, Messi, Dembélé nommés, Bonmati absente de la sélection
france24fr.description: Les joueurs Kylian Mbappé, Lionel Messi et Ousmane Dembélé figurent parmi les 30 nommés pour le Ballon d'or 2026, qui sera décerné le 26 octobre. En revanche, la triple lauréate Aitana Bonmatí ne fait pas partie de la sélection féminine dévoilée mardi par les organisateurs.

nzz.title: Die Mountainbike-Weltmeisterin Sina Frei findet den Flow – weil ein Sturz ihr neue Perspektiven zeigt
nzz.description: Die 29-jährige Zürcherin erlebt nach Olympiasilber 2021 komplizierte Jahre. Nach einem Trainerwechsel und zwei Operationen im Winter gelingt ihr nun die erfolgreichste Saison der Karriere.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der Fall VW ist auch der Fall Deutschland. Die Lage ist ernst, aber nicht hoffnungslos
nzz.description: Kein Unternehmen steht so sinnbildlich für den Erfolg deutscher Industrie, keines so für ihre schwere Krise: Warum der Volkswagen-Konzern dennoch eine Zukunft haben kann – trotz günstigen Konkurrenten aus China und hohen Standortkosten.

nzz.title: Mike Ashley ist ruppig, mit Billigsocken reich geworden und will Hugo Boss aufmischen – wer ist der britische Milliardär?
nzz.description: Er ist ein Selfmademan, der ein Imperium für günstige Sportbekleidung aufbaute. Seine aggressiven Übernahmen, seine Rücksichtslosigkeit und Trinkfestigkeit sind berüchtigt. Nun schickt er sich an, bei dem traditionsreichen deutschen Herrenausstatter die Kontrolle zu übernehmen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Keine Frauen im Eiffelturm? Europa muss seine Werte gegen Fanatiker verteidigen
nzz.description: Hinduistische Fundamentalisten wollten sich in Paris nicht von weiblichem Personal bedienen lassen. Das liessen sich die Angestellten nicht bieten und streikten – gut so!

nzz.title: Fit auf Instagram, schwach an der Rekrutierung
nzz.description: Stellungspflichtige in der Schweiz sind zunehmend weniger fit – trotz Sport-Boom. Woran liegt das?

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Schweizer Schüler gehören zu den besten in Europa. Doch mit den Deutschen verbindet sie eines: Sie werden schlechter
nzz.description: Die Ergebnisse der Pisa-Studie für Deutschland, Österreich und die Schweiz zeigen die Schwachstellen der Schulsysteme. Ein Vergleich in Grafiken.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die USA ignorieren das Öl-Problem, das sie mit dem Iran-Krieg selbst geschaffen haben
nzz.description: Die Welt hat ein Versorgungsproblem – nicht beim Rohöl, sondern bei Treibstoffen. Und tanken ist teuer, vor allem Diesel: Die Trump-Regierung hat nicht verstanden, wie der Ölmarkt funktioniert.

nzz.title: Ein Skandal um Kryptogeschäfte rechter Politiker in Polen weitet sich aus
nzz.description: Nach dem Konkurs einer Kryptobörse kommen dubiose Geschäfte konservativer Politiker ans Licht. Auch auf Präsident Karol Nawrocki fällt ein Schatten.

nzz.title: Was hinter dem stummen Blick der Generation Z steckt – und warum wir alle immer weniger reden
nzz.description: Laut einer Studie sprechen wir jedes Jahr weniger Wörter. Was bedeutet das für Geist und Gesellschaft?

nzz.title: Die Konservativen müssten die Demokratie verteidigen, fordert Roger de Weck. Aber sie dürften sich nicht mit der AfD einlassen
nzz.description: Bürgerliche könnten Rechtspopulisten am besten bekämpfen, schreibt Roger de Weck in seinem neuen Buch. Es ist ein Aufruf an Konservative, sich neu zu erfinden.

nzz.title: Der Goldpreis auf Achterbahnfahrt: Nach dem Rekordhoch kam der Einbruch – und nun haben ihn die hohen Staatsschulden wieder nach oben getrieben
nzz.description: Auf das Rekordrally des Goldpreises folgte Anfang des Jahres ein Rückgang um 27 Prozent. Aufgrund mehrerer Faktoren hat sich der Preis für das Edelmetall jüngst wieder erholt. Wie geht es weiter?

nzz.title: Eine widersprüchliche Organisation überlebt ihr schrumpfendes Gründermilieu: Wie die Caritas 125-jährig wurde
nzz.description: Die Caritas Schweiz entstand 1901 im Umfeld der katholischen Kirche. Seither schwankte sie zwischen Fortschritt und Konservativismus – und tappte auch in problematische Projekte.

nzz.title: Apple war einmal die beste Aktie der Welt. Kann sie der neue CEO wieder an die Spitze bringen?
nzz.description: Der neue Apple-Chef John Ternus muss die Aktionäre bei der Stange halten. Er versucht es mit neuen Produkten, höheren Preisen und Zurückhaltung bei KI.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ GEOPOLITIK» - 25 Jahre 9/11: Die eigentliche Tragödie begann danach – mit dem «War on Terror»
nzz.description: Die Kriege gegen den Terrorismus seien ein strategischer Fehler gewesen, der aus der Hysterie  und Panik von 9/11 entstanden sei, sagt der Terrorismusexperte Peter Neumann im Podcast.

nzz.title: Wimps galten einst als heissester Kandidat für die Dunkle Materie. Dann erkaltete das Interesse für diese Teilchen. Jetzt kehren sie auf die Bühne zurück
nzz.description: Es ist nur ein einziges Ereignis, das Teilchenphysiker mit einem unterirdischen Detektor gefunden haben. Aber dieses Ereignis hat es in sich.

observador.title: Conselho de Ministros reúne hoje com foco no Ensino Superior
observador.description: Um dia após o chumbo da moção de censura, o Conselho de Ministros reúne esta quarta-feira, em Bragança, com o foco direcionado para o Ensino Superior e o desenvolvimento do interior do país.

observador.title: “Musk” chegou a Veneza: 4 horas de retrato de um egomaníaco
observador.description: É um documentário de Alex Gibney sobre o homem mais rico do planeta e pergunta-nos: como é que uma só pessoa obteve tanto poder?

observador.title: Diogo Costa tentou salvar mas Haaland só quis arrasar
observador.description: FC Porto entra em falso na Liga dos Campeões com derrota com o Manchester City por 2-0. Ainda, Madalena Costa é Campeã da Europa em Patinagem Livre.

observador.title: Investigador sai da Anthropic, teme que IA destrua humanos
observador.description: Indica o Wall Street Journal, que Jacob Coxon abandonou a empresa por temer que a corrida tecnológica esteja a criar sistemas auto-aperfeiçoáveis capazes de escapar ao controlo humano

observador.title: 6h. Miranda Sarmento prevê "contas equilibradas"
observador.description: Apesar das medidas anunciadas ontem no debate da moção de censura, no valor de 800 milhões de euros, o ministro diz que há condições para ter "contas equilibradas". Ainda, a derrota do FC Porto (0-2).

observador.title: Na adolescência deixas de ser o herói dos teus filhos
observador.description: Rui Marques é psicólogo, meu amigo e pai viúvo de um adolescente de 15 anos. No outro dia demos por nós a falar do desafio que é educar crianças, procurando respostas, mas também as diferenças quando se faz isso sozinho com um rapaz ou e...

observador.title: Como os uniformes da escola voltaram a estar na moda
observador.description: De Eton ao Japão, das origens do kilt à cultura Pop com Britney Spears, voltamos aos bancos da escola e fazemos contas: quanto custa andar fardado?

observador.title: O Museu do Quartzo e o professor Galopim de Carvalho
observador.description: O Monte de Santa Luzia, arredores de Viseu, com o Centro de Interpretação Galopim de Carvalho, aberto em 2012, e as escavações que provaram a exploração no local desde as Idades do Bronze e do Ferro

observador.title: O corpo contra si próprio: o que são as doenças autoimunes?
observador.description: Cansaço persistente, dores nas articulações ou alterações inexplicáveis da pele podem ter muitas causas. Em alguns casos, podem estar relacionados com uma doença autoimune. Conheça os sinais de alerta

observador.title: Puccini e Verdi: dois italianos, dois bigodes e muita ópera
observador.description: Puccini deu mais trabalho, sobretudo pelo chapéu e pelo bigode. Verdi ficou com uma "expressão de zangado". Manuel dos Santos conta como retratou dois dos grandes mestres da ópera italiana.

observador.title: No Norte o passado e presente dos verbos soam igual. Porquê?
observador.description: Afinal, o minderico é apenas um código de comerciantes ou tornou-se uma língua real? O Marco Neves explica também por que motivo no Norte "falamos" e "falámos" se dizem da mesma forma.

observador.title: O dia mais difícil de Luís Neves
observador.description: Luís Neves enfrentou uma manhã dura no Parlamento e uma moção de censura desenhada à sua medida. Rui Pedro Antunes analisa a prestação do ministro, do Governo e do Chega.

observador.title: 4h. PS impõe quatro condições para viabilizar o OE
observador.description: Em Palmela, depois do debate da moção de censura, o secretário geral socialista enumerou condições para viabilizar o OE. Condições como, por exemplo, não mexer nas pensões são críticas para PS.

observador.title: 3h. Moção de censura ao Governo rejeitada no Parlamento
observador.description: Deputados do Chega pediram a demissão do MAI até ao ultimo minuto. Ainda, ex-ministro da educação lamenta que governo de António Costa não tenha antecipado resultados negativos agora registados.

observador.title: As notícias das 2h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: 1h. Governo garante que alívio do IRS é já em novembro
observador.description: O ministro das finanças, Miranda Sarmento não explica como vai funcionar a distribuição da redução do IRS, apenas deixa a garantia de que em novembro os salários vão aumentar.

observador.title: E agora a AfD na Alemanha
observador.description: Não foi só na Alemanha. No final do próximo ano, é muito provável que Marine Le Pen seja Presidente em França, o Vox deverá estar no governo de Espanha com o PP e Meloni continuará como PM em Itália.

observador.title: As explicações de Neves dão comichão de inquérito
observador.description: O operacional Luís Neves teve falhas éticas? Se sim, foi só porque a burocracia bloqueia quem quer fazer coisas. Eliminamos a burocracia, então!? Claro que não: borrifamos é para a ética.

spiegel.title: Freiburg: 74-Jähriger nach Messerangriff gestorben
spiegel.description: Ein Mann in Freiburg ist am Dienstagabend mit einem Messer verletzt worden, nun ist er gestorben. Es ist der zweite Messerangriff in der Stadt innerhalb weniger Tage.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Gesa Krause und Lea Meyer – Aussprache nach öffentlicher Kritik
spiegel.description: Bei der Leichtathletik-EM hatte die deutsche Hürdenläuferin Lea Meyer Teamkollegin Gesa Felicitas Krause kritisiert. Später entschuldigte sie sich. Nun gab es laut Krause eine Aussprache.

spiegel.title: Jemen: Huthis eskalieren Krieg gegen Saudi-Arabien, Uno warnt
spiegel.description: Sie sind einst als »Flip-Flop-Gotteskrieger« verspottet worden: Die von Iran protegierten Huthis attackieren Saudi-Arabien massiv, auch im Jemen selbst kommt es zu schweren Gefechten. Es gibt wohl Hunderte Tote. Die Uno warnt.

spiegel.title: Angela Merkel zu AfD-Sieg in Sachsen-Anhalt: »Mir blutet das Herz«
spiegel.description: Altkanzlerin Angela Merkel zeigt sich vom Ausgang der Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt schockiert. Das Ergebnis sei »ein wirklicher Einschnitt« in der Geschichte der Bundesrepublik.

spiegel.title: Zwei Kinder bei Unwetter von umgestürzten Bäumen verletzt
spiegel.description: In Baden-Württemberg musste die Feuerwehr in der Nacht zu zahlreichen Einsätzen ausrücken. Ein Unwetter hat in Freiburg Schäden angerichtet. Drei Personen wurden verletzt, darunter zwei Kinder.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Airlines fordern Konsequenzen nach über 1000 Flugausfällen
spiegel.description: Wegen einer technischen Störung bei der Flugsicherung sind in Großbritannien zahlreiche Flüge ausgefallen. Betroffene Airlines fordern nun personelle Konsequenzen – während Fluggäste weiter Geduld brauchen.

spiegel.title: Ashley St. Clair: Elon Musk soll von Ex-Freundin »Legion von Kindern vor dem Bürgerkrieg« verlangt haben
spiegel.description: Die Mutter von einem der 14 Kinder des reichsten Manns der Welt hat bei den Filmfestspielen in Venedig vor Elon Musk gewarnt. Sein Vorgehen werde »katastrophale Folgen« haben.

spiegel.title: AfD-Sieg in Sachsen-Anhalt: West gegen Ost - Zaun drum und ab nach Kasachstan! Echt?
spiegel.description: Trockene Flüsse, AfD-Siege, irre Spritpreise – über so vieles könnte man gerade sehr besorgt sein. Und die Deutschen? Widmen sich Ost-West-Zankereien im Stil der Neunzigerjahre. Echt jetzt?

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt live: Sepp Müller enttäuscht von Wahl Schulzes zum Fraktionsvorsitzenden
spiegel.description:
Zumindest in der CDU-Fraktion im Magdeburger Landtag bleibt Sven Schulze die Nummer eins – zum Unmut seines Rivalen Sepp Müller. Juso-Chef Philipp Türmer äußert derweil harte Selbstkritik.
Die Entwicklungen im Liveblog.

spiegel.title: Bildung: 25 Jahre Pisa-Schock – wie Deutschland heute dasteht
spiegel.description: Deutschland traf vor 25 Jahren der »Pisa-Schock«. Jetzt liegt die neue Schülerstudie vor. Und mit ihr stellt sich die Frage, was das Land gelernt hat.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump hat Assistentin Natalie Harp offenbar Geldgeschenke in Höhe von 45.000 Dollar gemacht
spiegel.description: Früher war sie Fernsehmoderatorin bei einem rechten Sender, jetzt ist sie der Schatten von Donald Trump. Der zeigt sich laut einem Bericht spendabel. Das könnte juristische Folgen haben.

spiegel.title: Ford: US-Regierung kritisiert Autobauer wegen China-Patenschaft
spiegel.description: Der amerikanische Verkehrsminister kritisiert den Autobauer Ford wegen der Zusammenarbeit mit chinesischen Unternehmen. Es geht um Batterietechnik, Sicherheitsbedenken – und um ein SUV-Modell.

spiegel.title: USA belegen 27 iranische Airlines mit neuen Sanktionen
spiegel.description: Iran ist stolz auf die vielen Airlines. Nun hat die Trump-Regierung mehr als ein Dutzend Fluggesellschaften sanktioniert. Die Revolutionswächter wollen derweil eine US-Unterwasserdrohne in der Straße von Hormus beschlagnahmt haben.

spiegel.title: Isar Aerospace: Erster europäischer Trägerraketenstart in den Orbit gelingt
spiegel.description: Im AfD-Erdrutschsieg ging eine Sensation unter: Eine Münchner Firma hat in Norwegen erfolgreich Europas erste Trägerrakete in den Orbit gestartet. Ein ökonomischer Urknall.

spiegel.title: Elizabeth Holmes: Haben die Macher der Doku »You Can See Everything« den Trailer neu erfunden?
News: Generaldebatte, Friedrich Merz, AfD, Tech-Konzerne, US-Demokraten, EUDI-Wallet für digitalen Ausweis
spiegel.description: Der Kanzler und die AfD-Spitze treffen aufeinander. In den USA werfen sich Techkonzerne den Demokraten an den Hals. Und der Digitalminister will uns den digitalen Ausweis näherbringen. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochmorgen.

spiegel.title: Balkonkraftwerke: Wo es noch kommunale Förderung für Balkonsolar gibt
spiegel.description: Kommunale Förderprogramme für Balkonkraftwerke waren in den vergangenen Jahren in Mode. Mittlerweile sind einige ausgelaufen. Aber vielerorts gibt es noch Geld. Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Balkonkraftwerke: Warum jetzt ein guter Zeitpunkt für eine Mini-Solaranlage ist
spiegel.description: Haben Sie sich im Sommer auch gefragt, ob Sie endlich eine kleine Solaranlage kaufen sollten? Der Moment ist günstig: Die Preise sind niedrig – und mittlerweile lohnen sich oft auch eigene Speicher.

letemps.title: A Pékin, 50 ans après sa mort, deux mémoires de Mao cohabitent
letemps.description:

phys-org.title: Grooming-related messages reach almost two-thirds of children
phys-org.description: Nearly two-thirds of Australian children surveyed in a recent study received at least one form of grooming-related communication from a stranger online in the past year, while almost one-third reported receiving direct requests for sexual information or interactions.

phys-org.title: Chesapeake Bay underwater grasses increase 7%, buoyed by gains in salty waters
phys-org.description: Submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV), one of the Chesapeake Bay's most important indicators of ecosystem health, increased by 7% in 2025, according to researchers at William & Mary's VIMS & Batten School.

phys-org.title: A vicarious calibration model enables quantitative applications of Fengyun-3 satellite ocean color data
phys-org.description: Ocean color remote sensing is a vital tool for monitoring global ocean carbon sinks and primary productivity. However, the on-orbit calibration accuracy of satellite sensors is insufficient, and weak marine signals account for only approximately 10% of the signals received by satellites, leading to significant uncertainties in ocean color remote-sensing applications.

phys-org.title: Why does Southeast Asia keeps breathing the same haze—and can ASEAN do more to stop it?
phys-org.description: Southeast Asia has spent decades trying to tackle haze from forest fires. Yet every few years, the region finds itself breathing it again. The transboundary environmental problem has become a recurrent phenomenon in the region.

phys-org.title: New computational method pushes cryo-electron microscopy beyond traditional resolution limits
phys-org.description: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has become a powerful tool for determining the structures of proteins, viruses and molecular complexes at near-atomic resolution. phys-org.title: Tiny backpacks reveal the secret, sometimes circuitous migrations of small songbirds
phys-org.description: Squinting through my binoculars, I scanned the dense branches of a black spruce, trying my best to catch a glimpse of the thin legs of a small black, white and yellow songbird. I was on the hunt for a yellow-rumped warbler—a bird affectionately called "butter-butt" by birdwatchers after the distinctive buttery yellow patch of feathers above its tail.

phys-org.title: Why a wetter Tibetan Plateau still faces 'hot-dry' extremes: The roles of ENSO and the North Atlantic
phys-org.description: Since the 1950s, the Tibetan Plateau has experienced pronounced warming and wetting. However, an overall shift toward wetter conditions does not necessarily mean that drought risk has diminished. On the contrary, against the backdrop of continued warming, compound hot-dry events—characterized by the simultaneous occurrence of high temperatures and drought—have become an increasingly important climate risk across the plateau.

phys-org.title: Some black holes grow much faster than their galaxies
phys-org.description: Nearly every galaxy has a supermassive black hole. The few that don't have had theirs ejected during a galactic collision. That's because galaxies and their black holes have formed hand in hand. There is still some debate as to whether galaxies formed around the seeds of supermassive black holes or the other way around, but there is plenty of evidence to support the idea that the two evolve together.

phys-org.title: Searching for unknown fungi in the Norwegian mountains

phys-org.title: One of the oldest known 3D animal fossils found in Norwegian sheep field

phys-org.title: Action on climate and air pollution likely to boost economy, UN says

phys-org.title: Germany's 15-year-olds post lowest PISA results since testing began 25 years ago
phys-org.description: The PISA study regularly assesses 15-year-olds' ability to understand and solve real-life problems in reading, mathematics and science toward the end of their compulsory education. It demonstrates the extent to which young people are prepared for the demands of a knowledge-based society and can participate in social life on their own terms.

phys-org.title: Researchers rewire ribosomes to specialize in one protein
phys-org.description: Every cell relies on ribosomes, the molecular machines that read genetic instructions and use them to assemble proteins. A cell needs thousands of types of proteins at any one time, so ribosomes must be generalists, capable of using instructions to produce any protein.

phys-org.title: When disaster strikes, what happens to our pets?
phys-org.description: As large-scale disasters—including earthquakes, torrential rains, typhoons and wildfires—become increasingly frequent, ensuring that pets as well as their owners can evacuate safely and receive appropriate care has become an important part of disaster preparedness.

phys-org.title: Tiny molecular rings open new ways for designing better medicines
phys-org.description: Cyclopropanes are organic chemistry's smallest rings. Three carbon atoms are joined in a triangle, creating a compact and unusually strained structure. Despite—or partly because of—this unusual geometry, cyclopropanes are found in many biologically active natural products and have important applications in medicines and drug discovery, from antidepressants to antibiotics and antiviral research.

phys-org.title: Prehistoric builders hauled 25-tonne stones at least 18 km to build iconic Devil's Arrows
phys-org.description: New research has revealed that ancient builders deliberately transported enormous 25-tonne stones across at least 18 kilometers (11 miles) to build Britain's tallest surviving prehistoric stone row—the iconic Devil's Arrows.

phys-org.title: Untangling the meta-biomaterial puzzle one property at a time
phys-org.description: From repairing damaged tissues to developing better implants, many medical developments depend on materials that can mimic the complex properties of human tissue. Meta-biomaterials are among the most promising candidates. By tailoring their geometry, researchers can create materials with properties similar to those of natural tissues. undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Security Depends on a Clear Electrification Target
proj-syn.description: The politics around electrification are beginning to shift in Europe as more people recognize its importance for economic competitiveness and industrial resilience. European Union policymakers should seize this momentum to embed a binding target of at least 50% electrification by 2040 in the bloc’s energy security framework.

proj-syn.title: The AI Race Could Sink US-China Détente
proj-syn.description: The competition between the United States and China to develop AI and deploy it globally poses the biggest threat to the two countries’ currently constructive relations. Without an ongoing AI dialogue to avoid escalation, a return to the zero-sum conflict that rattled both sides last year cannot be ruled out.

proj-syn.title: Are China’s Rare Earths Really a Potent Weapon?
proj-syn.description: The available evidence indicates that Chinese rare-earth export restrictions would cost the West far less than often feared, though this cost is impossible to estimate precisely in advance. This is forcing prudence on both sides, to the disappointment of geopolitical hawks and the benefit of the global economy.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Shock in East Asia
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump has alarmed his East Asian allies by canceling two joint military exercises with South Korea, a move that seems motivated less by whim than by a fondness for tyrants. The question now is whether South Korea and Japan will set aside historical resentments for the sake of mutual interests.

proj-syn.title: Building a Resilient Nepal
proj-syn.description: After Japan’s 2011 Fukushima nuclear disaster, the Japanese government changed the building codes for schools and housing and rethought the placement of critical infrastructure. Nepal (and other vulnerable countries) must pursue a similar approach.

proj-syn.title: Unpaid Work in the AI Age
proj-syn.description: Unpaid work, such as dealing with government bureaucracy and private-sector administration, consumes a huge amount of people's free time. While AI tools have the potential to change this, with important implications for the economy, predictions about AI’s impact tend to focus exclusively on paid work.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Wellness Industry Is Hijacking Women’s Health
proj-syn.description: Menopause and perimenopause, long under-researched and dismissed, have become a growth industry for online advertisers and wellness companies. Mining intimate data, this lucrative digital ecosystem exploits medical uncertainty to sell women hormones and supplements they don't need, or that can even harm them.

proj-syn.title: Who Controls the Data Controls the Future
proj-syn.description: While AI is becoming increasingly central to finance, defense, health care, and public administration, it depends on resources most governments do not control: the data used to train it and the compute that processes it. Unless this changes, countries will remain subject to decisions made in boardrooms they cannot influence.

proj-syn.title: Will Europe Be as Unprepared as Ukraine Was?
proj-syn.description: With Russia ramping up its hybrid war, Europe must choose. It can invest in its own defense, accept the trade-offs involved, and build credible deterrence, or it can continue to underspend, hope that diplomacy will suffice, assume that US protection will always be available, and tell itself that the war in Ukraine is a local affair.

proj-syn.title: The Case for a Cashflow Tax
proj-syn.description: In the context of the US economy, a cashflow tax would offer far-reaching benefits in promoting economic growth, taxing rents, and raising incremental revenue efficiently. Moreover, well-known concerns about complexity and fairness are easily addressed.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh’s Best Move Is to Do Nothing
proj-syn.description: Beholden to mainstream economic ideas, the new US Federal Reserve chair has committed himself, and his reputation, to a goal he cannot achieve. Reining in inflation requires not interest-rate adjustments but much larger strategic shifts that are not within the Fed’s power to influence.

proj-syn.title: How Developing Countries Can Do More With Less
proj-syn.description: Evaluation frameworks for development projects have long been influenced by donor priorities. But foreign-aid cuts have created an opportunity for African countries to implement equitable evaluation practices, both to channel limited resources more effectively and to shape the future of global development governance.

proj-syn.title: America’s Naval Disaster
proj-syn.description: Plagued by exorbitant costs and chronic delays, American shipbuilders cannot produce enough vessels to keep pace with China. US President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the industry does little to address its underlying problems and threatens to squander hundreds of billions of dollars.

proj-syn.title: America’s Un-American AI Companies
proj-syn.description: The United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society: democratic oversight, the rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate. But that won’t happen as long as American AI companies aggressively lobby against accountability and cozy up to the state.

proj-syn.title: The Golden Bridge to Monetary Multipolarity
proj-syn.description: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world’s top reserve asset because it offers a solution to the challenges of a rogue America. But its renewed relevance also reflects how rapid technological diffusion and increasing dispersion of economic power are creating a more diversified international monetary system.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Natural Disasters Must Not Become Financial Crises
proj-syn.description: The dangerous flooding in Nepal and Tibet has demonstrated, once again, the need for prearranged disaster-risk financing to prepare for the economic chain reactions triggered by natural disasters. Asia’s policymakers must act now to help cash-strapped Nepal and strengthen other countries’ resilience before the next crisis hits.

proj-syn.title: Is AI Crowding Out Other Investment?
proj-syn.description: The AI investment boom has unleashed a wave of demand for capital just as savings are declining and interest rates remain high. As competition for financing intensifies, rising borrowing costs could squeeze non-AI firms looking to finance new factories, equipment, and projects.

proj-syn.title: India’s Resilience Depends on Diversified Trade
proj-syn.description: India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump’s return to the White House in an attempt to ensure that no single bilateral rupture will cause catastrophic harm. It should continue to expand its trade ties, while being wary of any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-à-vis third countries.
